g1.label: 1. Where did Lisa go?
g1.why: The text says Lisa travelled to New York.

g2.label: 2. How did she travel from Frankfurt?
g2.why: The text says she flew from Frankfurt, so she travelled by plane.

g3.label: 3. What did she visit on the first day?
g3.why: The text says she visited the Statue of Liberty on the first day.

g4.label: 4. What did Lisa think about Times Square?
g4.why: The text describes Lisa’s reaction to Times Square as exciting.

g5.label: 5. What did Lisa buy in Times Square?
g5.why: The text says she bought a souvenir T-shirt in Times Square.

g6.label: 6. How many days did they stay?
g6.why: The text says the family stayed in New York for five days.

g1.label: 1. Lisa ___ to New York (go)
g1.why: ‘Go’ is irregular: its simple past form is ‘went’, not ‘goed’.

g2.label: 2. She ___ the Statue of Liberty (see)
g2.why: ‘See’ is irregular: its simple past form is ‘saw’.

g3.label: 3. They ___ a yellow taxi (take)
g3.why: ‘Take’ is irregular: its simple past form is ‘took’.

g4.label: 4. She ___ a souvenir (buy)
g4.why: ‘Buy’ is irregular: its simple past form is ‘bought’.

g5.label: 5. Her brother ___ hot dogs (eat)
g5.why: ‘Eat’ is irregular: its simple past form is ‘ate’.

g6.label: 6. They ___ a wonderful time (have)
g6.why: ‘Have’ is irregular: its simple past form is ‘had’.

g7.label: 7. Lisa ___ postcards (write)
g7.why: ‘Write’ is irregular: its simple past form is ‘wrote’.

g8.label: 8. She ___ New York was the best city (think)
g8.why: ‘Think’ is irregular: its simple past form is ‘thought’.

g1.label: 1. The Empire State Building is ___ (tall)
g1.why: Short adjectives like ‘tall’ form the comparative by adding ‘-er’.

g2.label: 2. New York is ___ (big)
g2.why: ‘Big’ doubles its final consonant before adding ‘-er’: bigger.

g3.label: 3. Times Square is the ___ place (busy)
g3.why: ‘Busy’ changes y to i before adding ‘-est’ for the superlative.

g4.label: 4. Central Park is ___ (beautiful)
g4.why: Longer adjectives like ‘beautiful’ form the comparative with ‘more’, not an ending.

g5.label: 5. The subway is ___ (fast)
g5.why: Short adjectives like ‘fast’ form the comparative by adding ‘-er’.

g6.label: 6. Hot dogs are ___ (cheap)
g6.why: Short adjectives like ‘cheap’ form the comparative by adding ‘-er’.

g7.label: 7. New York is one of the ___ cities (famous)
g7.why: Longer adjectives like ‘famous’ form the superlative with ‘most’.

g8.label: 8. Lisa’s trip was the ___ holiday (good)
g8.why: ‘Good’ is irregular: its superlative form is ‘best’, not ‘goodest’.
